title: Glory to God That Walks the Sky
description: Glory to God That Walks the Sky in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 59, headed “Paradise on earth”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Glo-ry to God that walks the sky, And sends his bless-ings thro', That tells his saints of joys on high, And gives a taste be-low.

lines: Glory to God that walks the sky,
That tells his saints of joys on high,
Glory to God that stoops his throne
That dust and worms may see't,
And brings a glimpse of glory down
When Christ, with all his graces crown'd,
'Tis a young heaven on earthly ground,
And every sense I straight employ
The rose of Sharon blossoms here,
Cheerful I feast on heavenly fruit,
Pleasures that flow hard by the foot
But ah! how soon my joys decay,
And snatch the heavenly scene away
When shall the time, dear Jesus, when
That I shall leave those clouds of sin,
Up to the fields above the skies

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
